sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:1
items.html: Lo Mati in Keter, and then it is Mati in Hochma: For the male and female of the light of Keter refined to phase two, and then their posterior was annulled, and they bestowed the light of Bina to the vessel of Hochma, and it is Mati in Hochma, and the face of Hochma returned to its place as at first, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:2
items.html: In Bina, too, it is Mati, because of the Hesed that is there. That is, that Hochma turned her face downward and gave the male and female of Bina to the vessel of Bina, and it is Mati in Bina as well. And he explains the reason, “because of the Hesed that is there” — so that she may correct Hesed and bring it down to its own vessel, as above, page 329, the passage beginning “and then,” study it there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:3
items.html: Mati in Hesed, for then Hesed descends to its place. Meaning through the refinement of phase two that is in Bina to phase one, which is the aspect of the light of the five Hassadim belonging to the VAK, as above. And then the light of Hesed descends to its own vessel, and it is Mati in Hesed, and its face returned to its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:4
items.html: Lo Mati in Gvura, for Gvura rises with Hesed. For the whole light of Gvura is the aspect of the posterior and the VAK of the light of Hesed, as above; and since the face of Hesed returned to its place, the posterior that was in Gvura was annulled and returned to be included in the face of the light of Hesed. And then the vessel of Gvura is found to turn her face downward once more and to give the light of Tifferet, with the illumination of GAR, to Tifferet, as above, page 330, the passage beginning “and this is what he says.” And it is Mati in Tifferet.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:5
items.html: Lo Mati in Netzah, for the light of Netzah rises with Tifferet. This too is for the above reason, since the light of Netzah is only the aspect of the posterior and the VAK of the light of Tifferet; therefore, when the face of Tifferet returned to its place, it is found to draw its own VAK to itself — in the manner of Hesed, which drew the light of Gvura, and in the way of Hochma, which drew the ZON of Bina to herself.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:6
items.html:
Mati in Hod, for then the vessel of Netzah turns its face. For after the light of Netzah rose to the face of the vessel of Tifferet, it thereby turns the face of its own vessel into its posterior; for the bestowal of GAR, which before this had been detained in it in the aspect of the posterior, was inverted and now became the place of bestowal, like the face of the vessel of Hesed that now rules over it. And then it gives its remainder, with the bestowal of GAR, to Hod.
And now we have found the way to understand the Sefira of Hod of ZA from its source. And know that this Sefira is the axis upon which all the corrections depend and turn. And her vessel is the fifth and last of the five phases KHB, ZA and Malchut, that is, the original vessel of Malchut. For the four preceding Hassadim stand opposite KHB and ZA, and so the fifth Hesed, that is, Hod, stands opposite Malchut. And you already know that all those vessels of the second expansion are the vessels of the first expansion that were emptied of their lights, as above; and so the vessel of Hod is phase four of the first expansion, who was emptied of her light and left no record behind her, as above in Part 4, in the words of the ARI (Chapter 2, item 6). However, the light of Hod is not the light of Malchut, but the light of ZA, that is, what reached her from the remainder of Netzah at the time when it is joined with the light of the illumination of GAR of Tifferet. And more than that: it is the most important light among the Sefirot of NHYM, for from the side of the lights it is the aspect of the GAR of ZA, and not ZA itself, as above. And it is indeed more important than Netzah, for Netzah is of the aspect of the posterior and the VAK of the light of Tifferet, whereas Hod is of the aspect of the face of Tifferet, as above, since it has the illumination of GAR from Tifferet. And therefore Hod is called by the name of the fifth Hesed, being the aspect of the illumination of GAR that is in NHYM, as explained. And although from the side of the vessel it is phase four, which is the greatest judgment among the ten Sefirot, the main thing is the light in it, as is understood. And its light is now sweetened most of all, that is, by the illumination of GAR that is in Tifferet. And understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:43:7
items.html:
Hod turns its face to Yesod and illuminates in it. You already know that all this light that is drawn in Mati and Lo Mati, from Bina down to Hod, is the light of Hassadim, that is, the aspect of the level that emerged on the coarseness of phase one that remained after the refinement of Bina, as above. And the whole matter of the difference between Mati and Lo Mati arises chiefly out of the changes between Hassadim with the illumination of GAR and Hassadim without the illumination of GAR, as above. But in the height of the level there was no difference between them at all, for all of them are at the height of phase one, as above. And here too the Sefira of Hod turned its face into posterior, even though it had not yet made a complete refinement of phase one, but only annulled the aspect of the illumination of GAR in it, which is the face, and made the posterior into the aspect of face. But one must know here what the ARI writes further on: that the ZON that are in the vessel of Bina coupled and gave birth to a single Hey, so that the Vav that is within the Hey was given to the vessel of Yesod, and the Dalet that is upon the Vav was given to the vessel of Malchut.
The explanation of these words: at the time when Bina turned her face for the first time and refined from her coarseness of phase two to phase one, which equalized her face with the face of the vessel of Hesed, and then gave the light of Hesed to the vessel of Hesed, as above — then she also lowered the aspect of one light, born through a coupling of the male and female within her herself; and this light is the aspect of a Nukva, and is therefore called Hey. So that there descended into the vessels of the VAK, too, an aspect of male and female, just as descended to the GAR of the second expansion — where the male is the above light of Da'at, and the female is that light born through the coupling of the ZON of Bina, as above, which is called Hey, as above. And all these lights that come and are born through a coupling, the ARI calls by the name of illuminations, as above in item 35, where he says that Hochma turned her face and illuminates to Bina. And likewise here, where he says that Hod turns its face to Yesod and illuminates in it. And likewise further on, where he says that so was the matter in all the VAK, that they turn their faces and illuminate downward. All of these are drawings of the lights that come through a coupling, and therefore he calls them by the name of illuminations.
And this is what he says, “that Hod turns its face to Yesod and illuminates in it,” that is, that there was as yet no complete refinement, only enough to illuminate the Hey of Bina to Yesod. And afterwards, when a complete refinement was made, then the light belonging to Yesod descended to Yesod, as is written before us.
However, this Hey, who was born of the ZON of Bina, is the beginning of the association of the quality of mercy with judgment, and it is therefore worth expanding on the understanding of her. And we have already spoken of the novelty that was made in the second expansion, that the light of ZA was emanated and emerged through Hochma and not through Bina, as would be fitting from the side of the ten Sefirot of direct light and as it was in the first expansion; and this novelty came about here through the exchange of the lights, as above. And besides this there is a further great novelty, for the light of Malchut was emanated through Bina and not through ZA, as in the ten Sefirot of direct light and as it was in the first expansion. And just as from the refinement of the male and female of the vessel of Hochma the light of Da'at was emanated and descended to the vessel of Bina, which is the light of Zeir Anpin, as above, so through the refinement of the male and female of the vessel of Bina the light of Malchut emerged — that is, the above Hey, who belongs to Malchut, since she is the aspect of a female light, as above.
And now you will thoroughly understand the difference between the light of Da'at, which is the light of ZA, and the light of the above Hey, which is the light of Malchut — namely, according to their emanation. For in truth, at the time when they were emanated, both of them emerged in the aspect of a level of phase one. For just as phase two of the ZON of the vessel of Hochma refined to phase one, which is the light of Hesed, as above, page 321, item 37, which is what is called the light of Da'at or the light of ZA, as written above, so likewise phase two of the male and female of Bina refined to phase one, and this is the light of the above Hey, who is the light of Malchut. And you find that the light of Hesed, which is the light of ZA, and the light of the Hey, which is the light of Malchut, are of equal level, for this and that are both phase one, since they came from the refinement of phase two, as explained. However, the difference between them is great, and it is like the measure of the difference of the ZON of Hochma from the ZON of Bina, which was explained above: that the ZON of Bina are the aspect of the posterior and the aspect of the VAK of the ZON of Hochma. And it is understood of itself that the offspring emanated from them are likewise as far apart as GAR from VAK; and the light of Hesed, which was emanated through the ZON of Hochma, is discerned as the aspect of face and GAR toward the light of the Hey, who is discerned as the aspect of posterior and VAK in relation to the light of Hesed, which is the light of ZA — that is, in likeness to the value of those that gave birth to them, as above. And understand this well.
And now we shall better understand what the ARI emphasizes above, page 322, item 38: “And indeed Bina did not turn her face to illuminate downward in Hesed, for there was no power in Hesed and in the VAK to receive so great a light face to face, but only back to back.” His intention in this is the above light of the Hey, which he calls by the name of an illumination because she emerged through a coupling, and not in the simple order of refinement and of the emanation of the lights one from the other, as written above and as the ARI writes further on. And on this he emphasizes that this light of the Hey did not come to the VAK before the seven lights that come in the simple order of refinement — in the manner of the male of Bina, born of the coupling of the ZON of Hochma, which came to the vessel of Bina before the light of Hesed came through the simple refinement, as the ARI wrote before this in item 35, study it there. And the reason is that, had the light of the Hey come before the refinement to phase one — that is, before the time of the descent of Hesed, in the manner of the above male of Bina — then the aspect of the level of the Hey would have been in phase two, for the coarseness of Bina refined to phase one only at the time of the giving of Hesed to the vessel of Hesed. And this is what the ARI emphasizes, “for there was no power in Hesed and in the VAK to receive so great a light”; for how could the light of the level of phase two come and clothe in the vessels of the VAK, which are phase one? Therefore Bina had first to refine from phase two to phase one, whereupon the light of the Hey, too, refined to the measure of phase one; and then both of them emerged, that is, the light of Hesed and the light of the Hey, and came to the vessel of Hesed, and this Hey passed from vessel to vessel until she came to the vessel of Yesod, where her place is, as written above.
And with this you will likewise understand what the ARI answers there, saying that Hochma was able to illuminate to Bina before she refined to phase one, since Aba and Ima dwell as one and emerge as one, study it there. He means to say that Hochma emanated and gave the male of Bina to the vessel of Bina before she refined to phase one, for the reason that the vessel of Bina is in truth a vessel of phase two, like the level of the light of Hochma, and therefore she need not refine and diminish her level down to phase one. This is not so with Bina toward the vessels of Hesed and the rest of the VAK, which are vessels of phase one; and how could they receive the light of the Hey while she still has a level of phase two?
And this is what he says, “and then Hod turns its face to Yesod and illuminates in it.” For it was explained that this Hey is discerned as a light of the posterior and as VAK; and therefore, since the face of Hod is of the aspect of the illumination of GAR, as above, she cannot bestow the light of the Hey, which is the aspect of the illumination of the posterior, as above, except through the turning of her face downward and her posterior upward — that is, that her posterior, which bestows VAK and withheld GAR, shall now be the bestower. And then she bestows the above light of the Hey to Yesod.
